candidates.summary: Cursor added Annotate to its design mode: users give agents visual prompts by editing elements, drawing on the page, and reviewing designs at different screen sizes.
facts: Cursor post: "Give agents visual prompts: edit elements, draw on the page, and review your designs at different screen sizes."
Cursor follow-up post: "Press Cmd+Shift+D in the browser to get started."
The announcement includes a 44-second demo video.

candidates.summary: LangSmith now tracks LLM cache hit rates for agents, as an overall stat, per thread, and over time in dashboard templates.
facts: Views listed in the post: overall hit rate as a single stat, a thread-by-thread breakdown, and a chart over time with dashboard templates.

candidates.summary: Hex released Hex 4.0, a from-scratch rewrite of its analytics platform for agents built on plain code instead of a proprietary YAML format, and raised $100M at a $1.2B valuation led by Peak XV and 137 Ventures.
facts: Hex blog (CEO Barry McCardel): the old agent harness "was becoming bloated with hundreds of tools", and external agents had to use Hex "through a keyhole via MCP".
Hex blog: 4.0 was "greatly accelerated by using agents to write all of the code"; its core assumption is "that everything is code".
Hex blog: $100 million round at a $1.2B valuation led by Peak XV and 137 Ventures, with Amplify, Avra, a16z, Redpoint and Sequoia participating; Hex has over 2,500 customers.
Harrison Chase (LangChain) on X named three lessons from the launch for anyone building agents: code as the backbone, UX built for reviewing agent work, and rebuilt core infrastructure.

candidates.summary: A paper finds that simple LLM harnesses that do not script the model's calls beat five published hand-crafted root cause analysis agents on 90 validated microservice failure cases.
facts: Abstract: the three simple harnesses (one call over an evidence package, a SQL agent and the Codex coding agent) reach PR@1 of 65-77% on three mid-tier models, versus 16-53% for the published agents and 6-39% for non-LLM methods.
Abstract: benchmark is RCAtlas, 90 validated cases from eight public datasets, across six models and three reasoning efforts.
Abstract: more reasoning effort changes accuracy by a few points at most while multiplying the time by up to seven.

candidates.summary: A security paper finds that when web services expose agent-facing interfaces, commercial AI agents carry out existing web attacks: 91% of 44 tested vulnerabilities stayed exploitable in the reference design, and interface design mattered far more than which agent was used.
facts: Abstract: VELA benchmark covers 44 vulnerabilities across twelve web application families; three commercial agents were tested.
Abstract: "the agent realizes every attack that direct interface invocation realizes in the reference configuration".
Abstract: interface design moved retention from 39% to 95%, against at most 4.5 points of difference across agents; in one case the agent completed an attack by supplying calls the attacker omitted.

candidates.summary: Skill-infinity is a method where a meta agent optimizes agent skills and also rewrites its own optimization skill; on 83 SkillsBench tasks it reports a 60.7% pass rate versus 56.4% for human-curated skills.
facts: Abstract: the meta agent "diagnoses execution traces, proposes candidates, requests independent reviews, and allocates the search budget".
Abstract: skills at both levels are standard packages loaded through native skill discovery.
Abstract: 60.7% pass rate on 83 SkillsBench tasks, compared with 56.4% for human-curated skills and 54.5% for SkillEvolver.

candidates.summary: Researchers (Singha Roy, Wadhwa, Durrett) measure "smoothing" in deep research agents: reports that read as confident syntheses but assert conclusions stronger than their cited sources support, across 7 systems and 4 datasets.
facts: Abstract: the model "discards the evidential 'jaggedness' of its corpus and asserts conclusions more decisive than the citations can support."
Abstract: introduces SmoothScore, a claim-level scoring pipeline; code and data are released.
Abstract: "Across 7 systems and 4 datasets, we find that agents consistently produce stronger claims than warranted."

candidates.summary: Anthropic reported early results from research partnerships with six drug developers (BigHat, Bristol Myers Squibb, Divergence Labs, Enveda, Generate Biomedicines, The Column Group), acquired the one-person company Mithril Medicine, and started its own drug programs.
facts: Anthropic: at Enveda, Claude reviewed 1,061 pages of manufacturing documentation, caught all 11 issues human reviewers found plus 7 they missed, and cut review time by 89%, from over 25 hours to under three.
Anthropic: Claude drafted a regulatory document in four hours versus about three months by hand.
Anthropic: for Divergence Labs, Claude generated roughly 35,000 antibody designs in about a month, largely autonomously.
Anthropic: BigHat made and tested about 1,010 Claude-proposed variants in about 10 weeks; the best bound more than 10x more tightly.
Anthropic: Mithril took a muscular dystrophy treatment from idea to promising mouse results in under 18 months; human trials could start as soon as late 2028. Most of the work is still preclinical.

candidates.summary: Anthropic signed a new OneGov agreement with the US GSA giving federal, state, local, tribal and territorial governments 40% off Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government and the Claude API, with no minimum spend.
facts: Anthropic: the discount applies across every product surface for the first time, including direct purchases now and cloud providers in the coming months.
Anthropic: about 500 US federal, state and local government organizations use Claude; weekly Claude for Government active users are up about eightfold since February.
Anthropic: the discounts are estimated to save the government $1 billion.
Anthropic: a US state IT director used Claude Code to document 12 legacy repositories, mapping 467 database tables and flagging 27 risks.

related.name: Anthropic: Expanding our partnership with GSA

candidates.summary: The Verge reports researchers are frustrated that OpenAI is using hand-picked expert "shepherds" to control release of its new claimed results on the Kakeya conjecture, the exponential time hypothesis and Yang-Mills physics.
facts: Verge: the math output (Kakeya conjecture in all dimensions) was released; the computer science result (a claimed disproof of the exponential time hypothesis) goes to an external group; the physics result has not been released.
Verge: Brown University's Brendan Hassett said the Kakeya claim "looks well supported" but he had not checked the Lean formalization.
Verge: IAS researcher Constantin Kogler: "It doesn't make any sense that first only a few distinguished scientists can look at them."
